title: Quant profile onboarding playbook and automated regression runbook for modern formats
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a repeatable, audit-friendly playbook for bringing new quantization profiles (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) into the profile registry and an automated regression runbook that detects perf/quality regressions early. Goal: remove ad-hoc onboarding steps, reduce manual verification time, and ensure rapid rollback or mitigation when a profile causes latency/cost/quality regressions in production or dedicated fleets.
acceptance_criteria: A documented onboarding playbook in the repo (docs/quant/onboarding-playbook.md) covering manifest schema, compatibility tags, and example profiles for INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ.
A CI pipeline (quant-ci-eval) that validates new profiles against the canonical validation matrix and publishes a signed profile artifact to profile-registry on success.
Automatic regression detection job that runs nightly evals and latency tests, raises a ticket when thresholds are exceeded, and triggers an optional canary rollback for Dedicated pools.
A dashboard (Console -> Observability -> Quant Profiles) showing p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-1M-tokens, and evaluation accuracy for each profile and model version.
Team runbook with clear on-call steps, Slack channels, and rollback commands documented in docs/quant/runbook.md.
checklist_steps: Define profile manifest schema (fields: name, version, model_family, encoder_hash, quant_format, quant_backend, supported_kernels, tags, signed_blob_sha256).
Create example manifests for each format: INT8, FP8, GPTQ (per-layer), AWQ.
Implement validator: scripts/validate_profile.py -> checks schema, runs light perf probe, runs accuracy eval subset.
Add CI job quant-ci-validate to run on PRs to profiles/ and require passing status for merge.
Wire publishing flow: on merge create signed release asset in profile-registry bucket and update registry-index.json.
Add semantic versioning policy for profiles: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH where MAJOR bump indicates incompatible kernel/runtime assumptions.
Document compatibility tags and fallback rules for Smart Router (e.g., fallback to <model>-fp16 if profile missing).
Create post-publish smoke: deploy to canary Dedicated pool for 2 hours with synthetic load and trace capture.
ci_jobs: pipeline/quant-ci-eval (nightly): triggers nightly-eval job across active profiles and compares to baseline metrics in metrics-store
validation_matrix: INT8: packer=gptq, backend=triton/onnx, supported_hw=[a100,v100], expected_p95_latency_delta<+20% vs fp16
FP8: backend=custom_fp8_kernels, supported_hw=[h100,a100], estimated_cost_savings>15% vs fp16, accuracy_drop<1.5% on benchmark-qa
GPTQ: per-layer calibration required, packer=gptq-tools v0.3+, expected_token_throughput within 10% of fp16 for batch_size>=8
AWQ: intended for LLAMA-like models, requires awq-runtime v2.1+, verify kv-cache correctness and quantization-induced token hallucination rate<0.5%
regression_detection: Nightly CI compares each profile's p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec to the previous stable baseline (7-day rolling baseline).
Quality checks run eval-set small-regression-v1 and compare key metrics (exact_match, rouge, model-specific QA F1). Alert if relative drop > 2% absolute or >10% relative depending on metric.
Cost/regression alert if cost-per-1M-tokens increases by >10% vs baseline or if throughput decreases by >15% for the same hardware class.
Statistical significance: require at least N=200 prompts for eval comparisons or use bootstrap to estimate confidence intervals; flag only if CI excludes 0.
Automatic ticket creation flow: quant-regression-bot opens GH issue + Linear ticket with CI artifacts and links to traces (tracing link) and example failure prompts.
Escalation: If production impact detected (error rate increase or latency p95 > SLA for >15m), trigger paging to infra on-call and initiate canary rollback.
rollback_policy: Canary auto-rollback: deployment controller will revert to previous signed profile if smoke errors > 1% or p95 exceeds threshold for the canary window.
Manual rollback steps: (1) open registry-index.json revert PR, (2) trigger profile-redeployer job, (3) monitor dashboard for 15 minutes.
Communication: post to #infra-quant with summary, link to incident ticket and rollback PR. Update status page if customer-facing degradation expected.
Post-mortem: if rollback happened for production traffic, schedule post-mortem within 72h and include root-cause, fix, and test additions.
